shouldFix.title: The candidate omits the D-056 gates-2/3 effect of recording the final three rider names
shouldFix.finding: D-158's adopted record says D-157/D-158 closed leftover-design for the ten D-155/D-156 classes, while EE-6b, EE-7c, and EE-7e remain capable-of-riding and unnamed at G09/G14/G16; on that standing, D-056 gates 2 and 3 do not hold. This candidate proposes the exact missing D-086 successor: it names those three classes at those three owner-bearing obligations. Its condition4Effect correctly states that the condition-4 named-identifier count moves by zero, but it never states the separate eligibility effect of later recording this successor. Recording it completes the remaining naming/successor work and makes D-056 gates 2 and 3 hold for DR-117. Gate 1 Class A still does not hold because D-137 recorded v5 with an express Class-A reservation, and gates 4 and 5 are not performed; therefore DR-117 remains not eligible in kind, not SATISFIED, and outside Class A. The predecessor gate-harness-naming.v6 itself states its gates-2/3 effect, so dropping this effect is not inherited house style.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: This is the substantive effect of the artifact, even though blueprint condition 4 does not move. Without it, a later recording can repeat D-158's now-stale statement that gates 2 and 3 do not hold, or jump from the final names to eligibility/Class A without naming the still-false gates 1, 4, and 5. Either result misrecords the exact boundary this successor changes.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The three placements, source properties, scope refusals, and all live quotations are correct, and the omitted result is reconstructible from the pinned COORD, v5, join v1, and live register. The subject asserts no false eligibility outcome; it fails to state a material conditional effect.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add an eligibilityEffect field stating that, if a later D-000 act records this candidate, D-056 gates 2 and 3 hold for DR-117 because D-157/D-158 closed the ten design leftovers, EE-3a is discharged by the already named DR-133 classes, and this successor names EE-6b/EE-7c/EE-7e at G09/G14/G16. State in the same field that gate 1 Class A remains false under D-137's express reservation, gates 4 and 5 are not performed, and the act neither makes DR-117 eligible in kind nor SATISFIES it nor mints a D-096 grant.

summary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. All three v1 findings are repaired: condition4Effect records zero naming-count movement and preserves MET as below QUALIFIED; current COORD is pinned with a remeasurement clause; and v5 plus monorepo-ci-contract.v16 are digest-pinned. All nine quoted claim/harness/owner values match live file 08 exactly, and the three placements remain exactly EE-6b at G09, EE-7c at G14, and EE-7e at G16. The mappings preserve their source properties: EE-6b is DISCLOSURE-ONLY honesty and not confinement, EE-7c is the self-contained offline TypeScript closure rather than role-set or useful-install ownership, and EE-7e is IR-1..IR-4 / G16-12 anti-lockstep evidence. The ten classes closed by D-157/D-158 are neither reopened nor named at these gates. Required-now stays 26, condition 4 stays MET at 30/30 owners and 26/26 names, no gate row is added, and the artifact marks nothing SATISFIED, opens no Class A, invents no D9 authority, and authorizes no implementation. However, the candidate omits its distinct D-056 eligibility effect: recording the final three rider names makes gates 2 and 3 hold for DR-117 while gate 1 remains false under D-137's express Class-A reservation and gates 4/5 remain unperformed. That material boundary must be explicit before acceptance.
